{{Short description|Swiss mathematician}}
'''Louis-Gustave du Pasquier''' (18 August 1876, [[Auvernier]] – 31 January 1957, [[Cornaux]]) was a Swiss mathematician and historian of mathematics and mathematical sciences.

==Education and career==
Du Pasquier studied at l'[[École Polytechnique]], the [[University of Zurich]], [[University of Paris|La Sorbonne]], the [[Collège de France]], and the Collège Libre des Sciences Sociales. He received his doctorate in 1906 from the University of Zurich with dissertation ''Zahlentheorie der Tettarionen'' under the supervision of [[Adolf Hurwitz]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=9704}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=Du Pasquier, L.-Gustave|title=Zahlentheorie der Tettarionen|year=1906|publisher=Druck von Zürcher & Furrer|url=https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/000469679}}</ref> Du Pasquier then taught at La Chaux-de-Fonds, Kusnacht, Frauenfeld, Winterthur, and Zurich, before he became a professor at the [[University of Neuchâtel]] in 1911. Du Pasquier wrote more than 60 articles published in scientific journals. He did research on number theory, probability theory, relativity theory, astronomy, and actuarial science.<ref>{{cite web|title=Du Pasquier, Louis-Gustave|website=Éditions Jacques Gabay|url=http://www.gabay-editeur.com/AUTEURS/D/DU-PASQUIER}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Du Pasquier, Louis Gustave (1876–1957)|website=IdRef|url=http://www.idref.fr/032885954}}</ref> He edited the 7th volume of the collected works of [[Leonhard Euler]].

Du Pasquier was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in 1920 at Strasbourg, in 1924 at Toronto,<ref>{{cite book|author=Du Pasquier, L. Gustave|chapter=Propositions concernant l'unification de la terminologie dans la numération parlée|title=''In:'' Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians in Toronto, August 11–16. 1924|volume=2|pages=975–981}}</ref> in 1928 at Bologna, and in 1932 at Zurich.
